title: Practice: Linux Firewall Fundamentals
prompt: Create a short, reviewable lab note or shell example for **Linux Firewall Fundamentals**. Use read-only commands or a disposable Linux VM/test directory. Explain the goal, record expected and observed output/status, test one boundary or failure case, and state which parts depend on the distribution or installed version. Do not submit secrets or use a production machine for state-changing steps. CodeLeaf does not run Bash submissions inside its web process; use a local test environment or an isolated runner.

starter.execution_mode: manual-terminal; requires a local Linux environment, disposable VM, or separately isolated runner
starter.starter:
# Practice: Linux Firewall Fundamentals
# 1. Inspect before changing anything.
# 2. Use synthetic input or a disposable environment.
# 3. Record expected output, observed output, and exit status.
# 4. Test one boundary/failure case and document platform assumptions.

public_tests.name: Topic alignment
public_tests.note: Lightweight text gate looks for the token 'firewall'; it does not prove the example runs correctly.

acceptance_criteria: The work demonstrates a concept from the lesson rather than only repeating its title.
A safe, repeatable test uses synthetic data or a disposable environment.
Expected and observed behavior are compared; include status or error behavior where relevant.
One boundary, failure mode, or compatibility limitation is documented.
hints: Start with a read-only inspection and the local manual page.
Keep each test small and capture output before adding extra steps.
Treat a text check as a preliminary gate only; execution correctness needs a safe local test or isolated runner.

retry_policy.guidance: Review feedback, improve the example or explanation, and resubmit. Passing the text gate is not proof of runtime correctness.

expected_output: A reviewable note/script demonstrating the concept, with expected and observed output/status, one tested edge case, and stated environment limitations.
status_note: Draft practical exercise. The grading gate is intentionally lightweight; review and local execution in a safe environment are required before publication.
